doc.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020

title: First jazz record: Harry Edison's Sweets album
summary: At 14 or 15 he buys a record in a new shop because of Sweets Edison's face on the cover.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was your first jazz record that you listened when you were young?

Well in my small town I was maybe 15 or 16 years old, 15 I guess, no 14. And there was a new shop that opened nearby my parents’ house. And it was a very small shop and they started to sell, what you call it, equipment. Sound equipment. And just a few records. And I remember there may be three boxes of LPs. And I saw something saying jazz there. They had classical, rock or pop, and jazz. So I didn’t know — at that time I didn’t know anything about it. Some friends told me you should investigate it, because I used to play accordion for dancing parties. And I didn’t even move to the bass. And I remember that — I looked at the covers and they were beautiful. I love LPs because of the size of it.
And I saw, it was a black and white picture and it was filled up with the face of one guy. That guy was Harry “Sweets” Edison.

And I remember, I went to the cashier, to cash the record and the guy told me, he said, “Wow, you buy this record, do you know it?” I said, “I have no idea what this guy, what kind of music he plays, but the expression of the face for some reason I felt like he was doing that.”
That was a record under the name of Sweets, a quintet with Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis, Oliver Jackson drums, beautiful piano player Gerry Wiggins, and Major Holley on bass.
